decisions.reason: F3 suppresses the density arguments in both derivative multipliers, making f(k-exp(theta)) look like a function evaluation. This is a nonfatal notation defect: direct differentiation of the supplied mass gives f(k;theta)(k-exp(theta)) and f(k;theta)((k-exp(theta))^2-exp(theta)); the existing envelope bounds both absolute derivatives and has successive-term ratio tending to zero. Both multipliers are now explicit; normalization, finite second moment and the mean/variance conclusion are sound.

Thus every hypothesis of the moment lemma holds, Poisson(10) has mean and variance 10, and the two-point law has mean 10 and variance 100. This is a local repair review, not independent acceptance of my edit.
